desc: Ideation complete: binary search over the answer plus a greedy feasibility predicate is the primary approach; the optimal walk only needs to consider ending at the last or second-last index.
Implement `feasible(x)` with `need[i] = (x + points[i] - 1) // points[i]`, early exits, and move-count capping.
Encode the greedy left-to-right simulation using `cur_visits` and `next_visits`, including bounces with the right neighbor.
Handle right-end cases: stop at `n-2` when the last index is already satisfied; otherwise move to `n-1` and satisfy remaining last-index visits via bounces.
Implement binary search over `[0, max(points) * m]` to find the maximum feasible minimum score.
Confirm final complexity is `O(n log(max(points) * m))` time and `O(1)` extra space.
Run/validate the current implementation against the provided examples and edge cases (`m < n`, `n = 2`, `x = 0`, large `m`, tight move budgets); no failures found.
